title: no raw-byte bridges
summary: Full-function assembly, inline assembly, .word transcription, include-binary code, generated source copied from target bytes, and function stubs are not decompilation progress. A function counts only when human-readable C built with the identified original toolchain reproduces its target bytes. Authentic hardware or SDK assembly stays outside the C progress ledger.

title: verified matches are the only completion metric
summary: Structural similarity, decompiler output, successful linking, booting, and semantic equivalence are useful evidence but do not count as matching completion. Record function count and matched text bytes only after isolated byte verification and a full clean rebuild.

title: preserve immutable source provenance
summary: Never modify the source disc image. Keep all disc images, extracted executables, raw assets, generated assembly, and build products gitignored. Commit hashes and reproducible extraction instructions, not copyrighted inputs.

title: identify translation-unit toolchains
summary: Do not assume one compiler or optimization level per function. Establish candidate compiler families from executable evidence, then validate flags over address-contiguous translation-unit neighborhoods. Record all verified combinations and do not accept impossible per-function compiler islands as final provenance.

title: knowledge must compound
summary: Every durable compiler behavior, ABI fact, linker-layout fact, successful source-shape technique, and disproven lead belongs in this JSONL ledger with function names and evidence paths so later work does not repeat discovery.

title: assemble retail EE code with numeric GPR names
summary: The executable is R5900 EABI64, while the disassembler renders O32 aliases. Under GNU as -mabi=eabi several aliases name different or unavailable registers. tools/normalize_asm.py changes spelling only and the resulting zero-C load image matches all 970772 retail bytes.

title: text input sections use eight-byte subalignment
summary: At source boundary 0x00100488 the compiler object advertises 16-byte text alignment, but enforcing it shifts following retail addresses by eight bytes. Splat subalign 8 preserves 0x00100488 and yields a complete exact image.

title: BSS begins after a virtual-only 0x6c-byte gap
summary: The file-backed .sdata ends before .sbss at 0x001ED080. The generated grouped NOLOAD section must retain this proven virtual gap; otherwise BSS symbols are displaced.

title: first source candidate does not distinguish compiler family
summary: An empty C body for func_00100488 reproduces its jr ra and nop under both GNU EE 2.96 and SN Systems GNU EE 2.95.2 build 2.73a. Isolated and whole-image matches pass, but it is not promoted until translation-unit provenance is established.

title: early nonleaf probe distinguishes save widths and scheduling
summary: For func_00100100, GNU EE 2.96 emits the retail sd and ld return-address width but tested source shapes schedule arguments differently; SN 2.95.2 O2 matches the target's major instruction ordering but emits sq and lq. Neither probe proves the translation-unit toolchain.

title: SN GNU EE 2.95.3 build 1.36 matches the first discriminating code neighborhood
summary: Build 1.36 produces the exact scheduling and sd/ld return-address saves for func_00100100 and both contiguous wrappers at 0x00101490 and 0x001014B0. GNU EE 2.96 reorders the address load, while SN 2.95.2 build 2.73a uses sq/lq. The compiler family is proven for the promoted 0x00101490 neighborhood, not yet assumed globally.

title: GP-relative setters prove G8 for the first state module
summary: func_00101CA8 and func_00101CB8 compile to the retail three-instruction GP-relative sequences under SN GNU EE 2.95.3 build 1.36 with -G8. Under -G0 the compiler emits five-instruction absolute-address sequences, so -G8 is discriminating evidence rather than an inherited default.

title: large aggregate fields avoid false small-data addressing
summary: Declaring the floats at 0x001EDE30 and 0x001EDE34 as standalone extern scalars caused -G8 GP-relative output. Modeling them as the first two fields of a 16-byte vector at offset 0x30 in the larger D_001EDE00 CameraState aggregate produced retail absolute accesses; the vector width is proven by quadword-copy calls in func_00101630 and func_001018E8.

title: build source objects with the bundled historical assembler
summary: SN GCC 2.95.3 build 1.36 emits move pseudos that its bundled GNU assembler 2.9-ee-991111b encodes as daddu, matching retail; modern GNU as encodes the same pseudos as or. Historical objects become acceptable to modern ld after objcopy removes obsolete .mdebug and rewrites symbol-table metadata; text and relocations remain unchanged.

title: camera motion block requires one source unit
summary: Seventeen contiguous functions reproduce all 1236 object-text bytes at 0x001017F0-0x00101CC4 under SN GCC 2.95.3 build 1.36 with -O2 -G8 and the historical assembler option -G0. Source-local small data remains GP-relative while half-pi is constructed inline; the linker then supplies four bytes of proven input alignment before 0x00101CC8.

title: camera source owns the first aligned small-data block
summary: The camera source unit defines the 16 bytes at 0x001EC880 as -999.0f, two zero floats, and a zero state word. Keeping the complete aligned block in source prevents the following generated small-data object from shifting and preserves all retail GP offsets in the exact full-image build.

title: const scalar pointer preserves camera accumulation scheduling
summary: func_00101AD0 matches when its parameter is const float pointer. Modeling the parameter as a Vec3f pointer changes the compiler's alias assumptions and instruction schedule; compiling with -G0 also rejects the retail GP-relative accesses.

title: later camera helpers form three exact source units
summary: The snapshot pair at 0x00103AD0-0x00103C10, four object helpers at 0x00103CF8-0x00103DD0, and the resource pair at 0x00104178-0x001041D8 reproduce complete 320-byte, 216-byte, and 96-byte object-text ranges. SN build 2.73a rejects each nontrivial unit; the resource unit additionally requires compiler -G8 with historical assembler -G0.

title: camera snapshot aggregate requires 16-byte alignment
summary: The snapshot unit reproduces the retail aggregate-copy schedule when CameraState is declared with 16-byte alignment. The complete 320-byte unit and its negative compiler control establish this as object-layout evidence rather than an isolated spelling trick.

title: candidate discovery and promotion are separate states
summary: The batch verifier can recheck many exact full-range candidates, while the ranked queue selects low-complexity work without mutating proof ledgers. Batch success establishes exact candidate bytes only; local compiler provenance, source-unit boundaries, full-image reconstruction, and public audit remain required before promotion.

title: resource-record unit uniquely selects build 1.36 G8
summary: Ten natural C functions reproduce the complete 300-byte range at 0x00137EA0-0x00137FCC including four internal alignment words. SN GCC 2.95.3 build 1.36 at -O2 -G8 matches; GCC 2.96, both configured -G0 profiles, and SN GCC 2.95.2 build 2.73a at -G8 reject.

title: candidate integration is transactional and fail closed
summary: tools/merge_candidates.py rejects unknown ranges, profiles, bridge markers, inconsistent shared units, missing promotion evidence, and unpromoted candidates without blockers. It retains ledger and split changes only after the exact full-image build, independent baseline, README progress regeneration, and public audit all pass; failures restore every modified tracked metadata file.

title: parallel discovery is leased, resumable, and non-authoritative
summary: tools/campaign.py assigns expiring function claims, builds ignored work packets, and caches compiler experiments by source and proof inputs. Exact results still enter the public tree only through an independent tools/merge_candidates.py replay and its complete rollback-protected gates; ambiguous compiler matches require an explicitly reviewed build profile.

title: candidate profile claims are independently replayed
summary: tools/merge_candidates.py invokes tools/match.py itself for every claimed profile using the exact source, complete source-unit range, and reviewed object flags. Unknown flags, a failed byte comparison, or an ABI-dangerous compiler diagnostic reject the import before any ledger changes, so candidate-authored verified_profiles and evidence strings are not accepted as proof by themselves.

title: exact source uses one public match tier
summary: Readable C counts when it matches the complete isolated function or source-unit range and survives the exact full-image rebuild. Compiler-generation or historical source-file ambiguity remains recorded as provenance evidence but does not create a lower public tier. Raw-byte bridges, assembly transcriptions, partial comparisons, semantic-only code, and verifier weakening remain prohibited.

title: bounded symbolic recovery scales branch-free leaf matching
summary: A symbolic pass can translate branch-free retail instructions into readable statements, enumerate the finite declaration and independent-statement order choices, compile each source candidate, and retain only complete-range byte matches. This recovered 112 functions without embedding opcodes, transcribing assembly into source, or weakening match authority.

title: five leaf-boundary ranges compile as exact combined units
summary: Readable C reproduces the complete emitted ranges 0x0012FC88-0x0012FCC0, 0x0014B4A0-0x0014B4C0, 0x00178248-0x0017826C, 0x0017F9A0-0x0017F9B8, and 0x0019A7D8-0x0019A83C, including internal alignment. The first, second, and fifth match all four historical 2.95.x profiles; the other two select G8 but not compiler build.

title: single-forward-conditional recovery needs delay-slot and path-liveness semantics
summary: For a function with one forward conditional, branch operands must be captured before the delay-slot instruction executes, values defined only in the guarded path must not remain live in the common tail, and a guarded jr ra makes the tail an else path. Modeling these rules plus the R5900 three-operand multiply recovered 41 further complete-range exact functions.

title: the small-data threshold is two-sided and yields three retail addressing forms
summary: GCC emits .extern sym,N and picks pseudo versus explicit lui/%lo by comparing N with its own -G, while the assembler picks GP-relative versus absolute by comparing N with its -G. A four-byte scalar is GP-relative, an eight-byte object assembled -G4 gives the same-register lui/%lo form that no single-threshold spelling reaches, and an object larger than eight bytes gives the two-register form. Proved on func_0014FF10; objects larger than eight bytes never match because the compiler then shares the base register (func_00181EB8).

title: retail carries two register-precision regimes and the upper one is unreached
summary: Below about 0x00184918 retail spills callee-saved registers with sq/lq on sixteen-byte slots, matching SN builds 2.73a and 1.36. From about 0x001855F0 upward it uses sd/ld with the same slot stride. For func_0018FFC0 build 2.73a -O2 -G8 reproduces retail exactly apart from sq/lq versus sd/ld and one downstream register choice. Both cc1.exe binaries contain a register_precision token and the diagnostic 'Register precision must be 32, 64, or 128', but no -m option or pragma spelling tried reaches it, and ee-gcc2.96 emits sd with the wrong frame layout. About 240 functions are blocked on this.

title: an eight-byte object read at offset zero needs volatile
summary: Without volatile the load is hoisted into the jr delay slot because the compiler still counts the access as one instruction; offset-four reads need no qualifier. Proved by func_001500C8 against func_0015EDC0.

title: long is eight bytes and long long is sixteen
summary: A retail sd/ld field must be spelled long; long long produces sq and por. Proved by func_0018E608 and func_00198F58.

title: independent trailing stores are reordered by the compiler
summary: For stores written in ascending order the emitted order is first, last, second, third and so on, with the second-to-last landing in the jr delay slot. Reorder the source rather than the struct. Proved by func_00182EA8 and func_00195F50.

title: branch-likely delay slots belong to the taken path only
summary: beql and bnel execute their delay slot only when taken, so its statements must be attached to the taken branch. Ordinary conditional branches read their comparison operands before the delay slot runs and execute it on both paths. Both rules were required before any structured recovery matched.

title: the bundled Ps2EeAs assembler, not GNU as, expands delay-slot small-data pseudos
summary: Each SN toolchain ships Ps2EeAs.exe beside as.exe. The compiler emits a bare small-data pseudo and leaves expansion to the assembler; when the pseudo lands in a branch delay slot Ps2EeAs emits the one-instruction GP-relative form while GNU as emits the two-instruction absolute macro and warns. Retail contains the GP-relative form, which is why one symbol can show both addressing modes in a single function from identical compiler output. Proved on func_00117268 and registered as profile ee-gcc2.95.3-136-O2-G8-ps2as.

title: a sharp callee-saved spill-width boundary at 0x001855F0 marks the SDK frontier
summary: tools/regime_scan.py derives from the zero-C baseline that 705 functions spill $s0-$s7 with sq at 128-bit register precision and 255 use sd at the same sixteen-byte slot stride. Every sq function except two lies below 0x001855F0 and every sd function lies above it; the last sq function is 0x00185218. Reading of the upper region agrees: IEEE float/double pack-unpack, libm kernels, a VU0 vector library, a C runtime with a FILE vtable, string and memory routines, an errno layer, SIF/DMA code and the kernel syscall stubs. The frontier is provisionally 0x00185400, game code below and SDK above.

title: parallel discovery requires isolated build state
summary: Ignored discovery lanes may run concurrently, but config/splat.us.yaml, generated asm, and build outputs form one transaction state. Full-image integration must run serially on the current committed base or inside an isolated clone, then transfer only the gated commit. This prevents concurrent split generation from producing false linker failures or lost ledger updates.

title: whole-image linking mirrors isolated address-symbol resolution
summary: Natural C can introduce address-named extern aliases that are not present in Splat's generated undefined-symbol files. tools/build.py derives only unresolved names ending in an eight-digit address and defines them at that encoded address, matching the deterministic rule already used by tools/match.py; the final 970772-byte image comparison remains authoritative.

title: the library region was built by Sony EE GNU C 2.9-ee-991111-01, not a patched SN build
summary: Retail spills callee-saved registers with sq on sixteen-byte slots below about 0x00185400 and with sd at the same stride above it. The upper regime is Sony EE GNU C 2.9-ee-991111-01, which produces that natively; both SN builds spill 128 bits and Sony 3.2 uses an eight-byte stride. Proved on func_0018FFC0. The same compiler also emits frameless sibling calls (func_001856F8), retiring that blocker. An earlier investigation correctly proved no SN switch reaches 64-bit precision and proposed patching cc1.exe; that was the wrong conclusion because the region was never built by the SN compiler. Identify the compiler rather than patching one.

title: post-incremented packet prefixes preserve the retail register split
summary: The three byte-identical 64-byte packet initializers match when the 16-byte prefix pointer is post-incremented into the following header. GCC retains the old pointer in v1 and advances a0 for the header, reproducing retail. Writing the same fields through direct byte offsets removes that register split and does not match.

title: bounded assignment-order search can recover duplicated packet builders
summary: For independent structure stores, enumerate only readable source assignment order and argument-to-field placement, compile every variant with the proven historical profile, and retain only complete-range matches. A 96-variant bound found the packet-family schedule after 74 attempts; the source remains semantic C and the ordinary byte comparator remains authoritative.

title: Sony runtime objects require the historical GNU assembler
summary: Sony EE GNU C 2.9-ee-991111-01 emits move pseudos that the era-correct bundled GNU assembler encodes as retail daddu. Modern GNU as encodes the same pseudos as or. Recording the historical assembler in the Sony profile makes three natural word-copy loops exact without changing their source and preserves every earlier Sony-profile match.

title: the assembler -G threshold is continuous and the eight-byte declaration trick is retracted
summary: GCC at -G8 marks an external small when 0 < size <= 8 and emits a pseudo plus .extern sym,N; the bundled GNU as expands absolutely iff N > its own -G, and -G is continuous, so -Wa,-G3 makes a true four-byte object absolute beside GP-relative two- and one-byte neighbours. Ps2EeAs ignores -G and expands everything absolutely except in a branch delay slot. The earlier rule of declaring an eight-byte object at -Wa,-G4 is retracted: it over-declared at 97 sites, overlapped the next recorded symbol at 94, and every site is reachable with the true size.

title: a profile record proves far less than the ledger implies
summary: Recompiling every matched function under every profile shows 178 of 820 match exactly one profile, 621 are ambiguous and 45 match all seven; with object flags included only 32 of 820 are configuration-discriminating and the -G8 default never discriminates. The regional two-compiler claim survives: 271 SN-discriminating functions below 0x00185400 with no counter-examples, 78 Sony-only above it.

title: the hazard-nop dead end is retired by the bundled assembler
summary: func_001016A0 and func_00101748 were recorded as permanently blocked on three missing hazard nops after float-literal materialization. Both match under ee-gcc2.95.3-136-O2-G8-ps2as, which emits those nops where GNU as does not. The C was already correct; only the assembler was wrong.

title: a matched source can be replaced after every gate has passed
summary: Sixty-six ledgered sources were rewritten into INCLUDE_ASM stubs importing a header absent from the repository, while their entries still recorded isolated_match and whole_program_match. Every build gate runs before that rewrite, so tools/repo_audit.py now checks on each run that a ledgered source still contains C, and tools/merge_candidates.py rejects an invented address-named data symbol, which the whole-image link would otherwise resolve unfalsifiably.

title: Ps2EeAs honours -G and inverts GNU as behaviour
summary: At -G8 the bundled Ps2EeAs emits the one-instruction GP-relative form for a symbol the unit defines in .sdata; at -G0 it emits the two-instruction absolute form. The earlier claim that it ignores -G described only its -G0 behaviour. Proved over the 25-function camera unit at 0x00101490-0x00101CC8, which matches only under ps2as with -Wa,-G8.

title: match.py inherits ledger object flags when none are passed
summary: tools/match.py falls back to the reconstruction ledger's object_flags when --object-flag is absent, so --profile alone tests that profile with the function's landed flags rather than in isolation. This produced a wrong conclusion that camera_motion.c could not be built with Ps2EeAs: the run silently inherited -Wa,-G0. Always pass flags explicitly when comparing profiles.

title: the camera object spans 0x00101490-0x00101CC8 and owns its small data
summary: Twenty-five functions, 2,076 bytes of text plus a 16-byte .sdata block at 0x001EC880 and a 32-byte jump table at 0x001E6A00, all byte-exact under ee-gcc2.95.3-136-O2-G8-ps2as with -Wa,-G8. The unit is fully configuration-discriminated: every other profile and flag combination mismatches. Respelling the four .sdata words as extern breaks it, so the definition rather than any reference spelling is what constitutes the object. This supersedes the -Wa,-G0 GNU as attribution previously recorded for camera_motion.c.

title: a Sony-compiled function exists below the SDK frontier
summary: func_00158478 matches only ee-gcc2.9-991111-01-O2 despite sitting below 0x00185400, where the SN compiler otherwise holds with 271 discriminating functions and no counter-examples. Sub-frontier near-matches should be retested under the Sony profile before being recorded as blocked.

title: a dsll bitfield extraction encodes width as 32 minus the shift
summary: For retail ld + dsll N + dsra32 + andi, the extracted low field has width 32 - N, not N. The symmetric case at N = 16 hides the error, so the rule was recorded backwards and cost a wrong word before being caught.

title: blockers require mechanism-level proof
summary: Failed source spellings establish only that one search was exhausted. Record a blocker only when compiler, assembler, ABI, or linker evidence shows why the required output cannot arise, and retest unresolved candidates whenever a toolchain fact changes.

title: newlib wsetup.o and fflush.o have exact standalone boundaries
summary: Retail 0x00194950-0x00194A5C is newlib wsetup.c and 0x00195E48-0x00195F4C is newlib fflush.c from sourceware commit b0ba0ac21747fef4f150f2632aedf0f59e0ae03a. Both complete .text extents match only with the recovered Sony EE GCC 2.9 O2 G0 profile; the following four-byte zero in each case is linker alignment, not source-owned object text.

title: newlib vfprintf.o is an exact six-function source unit
summary: Retail 0x00193030-0x00194950 and its 516-byte rodata block at 0x001EBC20 reproduce exactly from upstream newlib vfprintf.c at commit b0ba0ac21747fef4f150f2632aedf0f59e0ae03a under Sony EE GCC 2.9 O2 G0, WANT_PRINTF_LONG_LONG, and the EE ABI eight-byte variadic slot rule. The unit contains __sprint, __sbprintf, vfprintf, _vfprintf_r, cvt, and exponent; this supersedes three provisional per-function source boundaries.

title: Ps2EeAs pads div.s against branch destination labels, and only div.s
summary: The bundled assembler applies a rule its binary states as "DIV related opcode too near branch instruction - Added %i padding NOP/s", measured against branch destination labels. At -O2 the SN driver emits no statement labels, so a profile without -g cannot reproduce a padded site; ee-gcc2.95.3-136-O2-G8-ps2as-g emits the $LM labels the rule needs. Measured over asm/cod by tools/div_padding_oracle.py: only div.s is ever padded, 478 of 999 sites, while none of the 1,640 div and 252 divu sites are touched. Run lengths are bimodal, 478 sites with no leading nop and 478 with exactly two and none longer, so the rule is binary; the 43 single-nop sites are compiler hazard nops and delay-slot nops must be excluded when measuring. All 18 sites above the SDK frontier are padded against 460 of 981 below. Treat a padded site as evidence that a statement boundary fell near the div and an unpadded one as evidence that none did, rather than as an unexplained two-nop difference. The 171 of 383 quoted in ea3feeb does not reproduce; prefer the tool.

title: a live argument register does not prove the intervening callee accepts it
summary: func_00198D68 and func_00198DE8 match exactly only when func_00199DA0 is declared with no arguments. The compiler prepares $a0 for the later dispatch call before invoking the initializer, and $a0 merely remains live across that call. Infer prototypes from the complete call schedule and matched sibling shapes, not from a register value visible at one jal.

title: destructive offset updates can decide the final MIPS destination register
summary: For func_0019AB68, a direct *(base + offset) store makes Sony EE GCC 2.95 materialize the sum in $v0 and misses two of ten words. Writing offset += base before the store reuses $v1 and matches the retail addu and store exactly. Sony EE GCC 2.9 still allocates differently, while both 2.95.2-273a and 2.95.3-136 match under -G0.

title: preserved Sony PS2 libgcc objects prove runtime source-unit boundaries
summary: The preserved ProDG for PS2 3.01 libgcc.a has SHA-256 8e7b39e41372e1692e0e0e2675614d47314d27f54d2da0bbd26e8e27bad60667. After normalization of obsolete object metadata, its dp-bit.o and fp-bit.o text layouts map directly onto retail. GCC 2.95.3 fp-bit.c logic reconstructs exact shared units at 0x00186188-0x001863A8 and 0x00186D90-0x00186FB0 under Sony EE GCC 2.9 O2. The archive is provenance evidence only and is never a build input.

title: the libgcc __main object requires its canonical macro scope
summary: Preserved ProDG for PS2 3.01 __main.o fixes the authentic retail boundary at 0x001855F0-0x00185718. GCC 2.95.3 destructor, constructor, and one-time wrapper logic matches all 296 bytes under Sony EE GCC 2.9 O2 G0 when DO_GLOBAL_CTORS_BODY retains its do-while scope. Flattening that scope swaps the constructor loop's saved-register allocation.

title: index by i * stride instead of advancing a hand-rolled offset
summary: Writing an address as i * stride lets loop.c strength-reduce it into a fresh induction variable, while advancing an explicit offset variable by the stride fights the scheduler and the register allocator. Two functions needed this. In func_001721A8 the explicit form put the offset's initialisation one slot early under four different placements; the i * 0xC0 form placed it in the loop preheader where retail has it. In func_0010F0F0 the explicit form cost the counter its register: local-alloc's update_equiv_regs doubles REG_LIVE_LENGTH for a pseudo whose first set carries a constant REG_EQUAL note, which cse attaches to a zeroed counter, sinking it below a large constant in the allocation order; the constant escapes the same treatment because this compiler splits a big immediate into lui and ior before scheduling. With i * stride the counter stays a plain biv, is not doubled, and takes a3. Reach for the natural expression before hand-optimising.

title: an int global holding a base address forces a reload every iteration
summary: Retail commonly reads a base address from an int global and adds a byte offset, rather than indexing a typed pointer. The distinction is visible in the output: a store through the computed address may alias the global itself, so the base is reloaded on every iteration instead of hoisted out of the loop. Declaring extern Ent *D_001ED6C0 and writing D_001ED6C0[i].field let the compiler hoist the load and left func_001721A8 seven instructions short; extern int D_001ED6C0 with *(unsigned int *)(off + D_001ED6C0) restored the reload. func_0010E608 and func_0010F0F0 use the same idiom, so treat a per-iteration base reload as evidence for an int global rather than a pointer.

title: short backward loops are blocked: retail pads to six, every assembler here pads to seven
summary: The R5900 short-loop erratum workaround is applied by the assembler, not the compiler: no cc1 in config/toolchains.json emits a nop before a backward branch under any of the nine profiles. Retail pads such a loop to a minimum of six instructions, so a two-instruction loop carries four nops; asm-baseline contains 63 such loops, every one exactly six long, and none sits in a reconstructed function. The bundled SN as.exe (one binary shared by 2.95.2-273a, -274 and 2.95.3-107, -114, -136) and Ps2EeAs.exe both pad to seven, and explicit nops in the source normalise to that same count. ps2eeas.exe from 2.95.2-273a is byte-faithful otherwise but applies no short-loop padding at all. No flag exposes the threshold. func_0012C3F0 is otherwise solved: its compiler output padded to six and assembled with a fix-free assembler links byte-identical. These functions cannot be matched until the SN assembler build retail used is obtained; inserting the nops locally would be the synthetic padding the knowledge book forbids.

title: the preserved libgcc archive fixes the complete soft-float object extents
summary: ProDG for PS2 3.01 libgcc.a fixes dp-bit.o at 0x001858A8-0x0018659C (0xCF4 bytes), fp-bit.o at 0x001865A0-0x00187180 (0xBE0 bytes), and _muldi3.o at 0x00187180-0x001871E0 (0x60 bytes). Every archive symbol offset in the two soft-float members lands on the corresponding retail function start; the four bytes before fp-bit.o are linker alignment. This proves artifact boundaries, not complete source recovery: stock GCC 2.95.3 fp-bit.c does not reproduce the preserved object, and only ledgered C ranges count as decompiled.

title: stale Splat matching fragments distorted function ranking
summary: The assembly collector let the last duplicate listing overwrite a full retail body. func_00196D24 was ranked from one instruction instead of its 224-byte SIMD routine. Retaining the longest listing and counting zero-branch aliases restores the static complexity signals; return detection also accepts numeric $31. This changes work selection only, never match authority.

title: four libgcc division routines share a three-word C multiplication frontier
summary: GCC 2.95.3 generic C division logic with a separate low-word multiply followed by the high half of an unsigned widening product gives correct-size candidates for func_001A16A0, func_001A1E80, func_001A24E8, and func_001A2AB8 under Sony 2.9 O2. Each differs in three words: retail multu/mfhi/mflo versus a low-word GPR-destination multiply followed by multu/mfhi. A single widening-product variable needs eight extra packing/extraction instructions. This is a measured unsolved frontier, not source-match progress or proof of impossibility.

title: indexed integer bases solve the 192-byte object-list family
summary: Nine readable C routines passed complete promotion on 2026-09-09. Integer-held D_001ED6C0 plus indexed 192-byte strides preserves retail alias reloads; count is at +16 of D_002D8840. The association cleanup also needs an integer link local and structure-indexed links access for register and address ordering. Most functions use SN 1.36 G8 with GNU -Wa,-G0; exact per-function assembler choices are ledgered. Separate files do not establish original translation-unit boundaries.

title: historical R5900 target macros recover both complete soft-float objects
summary: The archive-proven dp-bit and fp-bit objects now match from licensed macro-expanded historical C with NO_DENORMALS, FLOAT_BIT_ORDER_MISMATCH, US_SOFTWARE_GOFAST and FLOAT for single precision. Sony2.9 O2 is unchanged. Full promotion replaces19 previously matched function sources and adds11 functions3984bytes. Target source recipe investigation solved both families; stock GCC2.95.3 source failed. This supersedes the earlier source-recovery frontier, not its boundary evidence.

title: discarded integer return values affect SN register allocation
summary: Supported void-to-int declaration corrections solved func001711A0 and520-byte func001715D8. Callee158960 has exact C returns;158868 retail writes v0 on both paths. Consult actual callee evidence and old lane notes before local permutations. Do not blanket rewrite declarations:20 large candidate pairs yielded no additional exacts through return correction alone.

title: union global pointer accesses transfer across session state machines
summary: Prior jt3 notes establish a one-member union view of D001ED3C8 that preserves reloads after stores while permitting reuse across loads. Three recovered exact state machines3196bytes passed full promotion. Applying this normal alias model to149C88 removes all8 branch-difference words, leaving7 setup words after bounded420order+16type probes. No volatile workaround or ownership inference follows from matching alias behavior.

title: compile independent units once and reuse family evidence before permutation
summary: Fresh full-build benchmark improved81.94s to21.20s by removing unused duplicate assembly compilation and using4 concurrent jobs; identical970772-byte images. Candidate latency improved27-44percent across3 measuredprofiles. Every unit recompiles, failedworkers preventlinking, and promotion proof gates remain unchanged. family_queue links shared-global clusters to known exact source; clusters overlap.

title: lane notes point to exact manifests outside the lane directory
